bug_semantics: With address auto-creation disabled, an authenticated OpenWire client can request a non-durable JMS topic subscription for a nonexistent address. AMQConsumer creates a random, non-durable temporary queue on that address; the broker implicitly creates the temporary address after checking only queue-creation permission, not CREATE_ADDRESS. The unauthorized address persists until the OpenWire connection closes, when temporary resources are removed.
flaw_origin: 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3 introduced Artemis's independent CREATE_ADDRESS permission and explicit address model while retaining the OpenWire non-durable-topic path that creates a temporary queue and the server queue-creation path that implicitly materializes its missing address without a CREATE_ADDRESS check. Before this commit there was no independent CREATE_ADDRESS authorization boundary to bypass.
ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object: `git cat-file -p 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3` shows human author `jbertram <jbertram@apache.org>`, human committer `Martyn Taylor <mtaylor@redhat.com>`, subject `ARTEMIS-876 Remove all reliances on JMS prefixing`, and no body or Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailer; neither identity is a bot.
evidence: Apache's advisory at https://lists.apache.org/thread/4wlrp31ngq2yb54sf4kjb3bl41t4xgtp describes the exact OpenWire non-durable-topic attack, missing createAddress permission, disabled address auto-creation, temporary-address lifetime, affected org.apache.activemq versions 2.0.0-2.44.0 and org.apache.artemis versions 2.50.0-2.52.0, and fixed version 2.53.0.

At BIC 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3, `git show -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/security/CheckType.java` adds CREATE_ADDRESS and `git show -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/server/impl/ServerSessionImpl.java` adds the separately authorized createAddress method while createQueue still checks only CREATE_DURABLE_QUEUE/CREATE_NON_DURABLE_QUEUE before calling server.createQueue. The same commit's ActiveMQServerImpl diff implicitly adds a missing AddressInfo while creating a queue. `git log --reverse -S'CREATE_ADDRESS' -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/security/CheckType.java` identifies this as the first CREATE_ADDRESS addition.

The pre-fix OpenWire path is reproducible with `git show a2bb690e468d7956a4c83f10efa65f09a6d66f45:artemis-protocols/artemis-openwire-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/openwire/amq/AMQSession.java`: createConsumer invokes checkAutoCreateQueue only inside `if (openWireDest.isQueue())`, so topics bypass it. In AMQConsumer.createTopicSubscription, the non-durable branch creates a UUID-named queue on the requested address with durable=false and temporary=true.

Direct parent verification: `git rev-parse 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3^` returns 0bcde8140fb1f0927de58fcf856f3b449a2cdf5d; `git grep -n 'CREATE_ADDRESS' 0bcde8140fb1f0927de58fcf856f3b449a2cdf5d -- artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/security/CheckType.java artemis-server/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/server/impl/ServerSessionImpl.java` has no match. Thus the parent lacks the distinct authorization boundary whose omission makes the later behavior an incorrect-authorization flaw.

Fix 75f51f0198221355e694c4db31e74a268c963cd6 (`Check auto-create for OpenWire JMS topic sub`) moves destination checking outside the queue-only branch and calls checkAutoCreate for topics before AMQConsumer initialization. That reaches ServerSessionImpl.checkAutoCreate; when the temporary queue needs a missing address it calls createAddress, whose implementation unconditionally performs `securityCheck(..., CheckType.CREATE_ADDRESS, ...)`. The added JMSTopicSubscriberWithSecurityTest expects JMSException and verifies the address remains absent.

Release ancestry is direct: `git tag --contains 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3 --sort=version:refname` begins with 2.0.0. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 75f51f0198221355e694c4db31e74a268c963cd6 2.52.0` is false while the same check against 2.53.0 is true; `git tag --contains 75f51f0198221355e694c4db31e74a268c963cd6 --sort=version:refname` begins with 2.53.0. Annotated tag objects resolve to 70e319d6e3fbdd8e882d3f791a97050672af8a5a (2.0.0), 437105493d75b6156ba7bb1f77bae93de2182e30 (2.44.0), 0ae68ef46e4e12ae251cdebaa047f53b7bb78aff (2.50.0), 1e05c01410ea26e6fe832ededb3683df3ef83645 (2.52.0), and 21e513e7d72fa568086aa251461f8ec59f593df4 (2.53.0).

The split advisory ranges are a Maven coordinate rename, not a vulnerability reintroduction: tag 2.44.0's root pom uses org.apache.activemq, tag 2.50.0 uses org.apache.artemis, and 062e5a2d9371b2c8c4ac8b3aba5b9cc9320e4b31 is `ARTEMIS-5816: switch groupId and relocate + bump version for new TLP`.

BIC-only AI check: the raw commit object for 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3 has one parent, human author/committer identities, only the ARTEMIS-876 subject, and no AI/bot trailer or generated marker. No fix-commit or later-history signal was used for the verdict.
reasoning: The older OpenWire topic-subscription code is a necessary precursor, but before 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3 there was no separate create-address permission, so the advisory's authorization invariant did not yet exist. Commit 84e8a87325a976c9970b8e85d03fc33207623af3 is the smallest causal commit that established that invariant and simultaneously left implicit queue-driven address creation outside it; its direct parent lacks CREATE_ADDRESS. Later refactors preserve the same mechanism. The direct mainline fix 75f51f0198221355e694c4db31e74a268c963cd6 closes it by preflighting all OpenWire topic subscriptions through the auto-create path that enforces CREATE_ADDRESS. Because the introducer's own commit object contains no AI or bot signal, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
